t.13.1: The ease that arises from having nothing at all is hard to attain even for one who wears only a loincloth. Therefore, having abandoned both renouncing and acquiring, I abide as I please.
t.13.2: At times the body is weary, at times the tongue grows tired, at times the mind. Having abandoned all that, I abide happily in the true goal of human life.
t.13.3: Having reflected in truth that nothing whatsoever is ever really done, I do whatever comes to be done whenever it comes, and abide at ease.
t.13.5: Neither gain nor loss comes to me from standing, from going, or from lying down. Therefore, whether standing, going, or sleeping, I abide at ease.
t.13.4: Yogins who dwell in the body are given to insisting on action or on non-action; but because I am free of both union and separation, I abide as I please.
t.13.6: For me there is no loss while sleeping, nor gain while striving; therefore, abandoning both loss and elation, I abide as I please.
t.13.7: Having observed again and again the fixed law within the states of being, which take the forms of pleasure and the rest, and having therefore given up both good and bad, I abide as I please.
